:::{#thm-bernoulli-score-contribution}
#### Score contribution of one binary outcome

If $\Outvar_\iobs \sim \Ber(\prob)$ has observed value $\outvar_\iobs \in \cb{0, 1}$
and [precision](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-precision) $\precision = 1 / \Var{\Outvar_\iobs} = 1 / \paren{\prob(1 - \prob)}$,
its [score](#def-score) contribution is the precision times the [deviation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-deviation-pop-mean) $\devn_\iobs \eqdef \outvar_\iobs - \prob$ of $\outvar_\iobs$ from its mean $\prob$:

$$\score_\iobs(\prob) = \precision \devn_\iobs$$

The precision $\precision$ is the same for every $\iobs$, because all $\Outvar_\iobs$ share the [event](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-event) [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $\prob$.

:::

::: proof

The score contribution as $(\outvar_\iobs - \prob) / \paren{\prob(1 - \prob)}$ is the solution to @exr-bernoulli-score-contribution,
worked in @sol-bernoulli-score-contribution.
The form in terms of the [deviation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-deviation-pop-mean) is the solution to @exr-bernoulli-score-contribution-deviation,
worked in @sol-bernoulli-score-contribution-deviation.

:::
